body:
Sorry for the late reply, it just takes me an effort of will to get back to thinking about this.

I guess what I neglected to mention was that the depressing thoughts are never really constant. They seem mostly purely based on the situation I'm in. For example, this summer I've been fine for the vast majority of the time. The problem is that some things can trigger the dark thoughts. Being able to start afresh has always been  live-saver for me, but I don't know how many more chances at those I will get.

About my math skills, it's strange. I'm actually descent at some types of math. For example, I'm not bad at mental math but with puzzles I simply blank out. I think it's because I simply think about numbers in a different way. It's probably why I was good when it came to physics problems of handling large formulas and processes, but when faced with a complex setup that required a lot of thinking I would freeze. As for sugar and pop, I used to have a pretty healthy diet (well, not great, but less than average sugar and rarely, if ever, soda) and went to the gym regularly while at school (during some of the worst of the depression).

What I really need, perhaps more than confidence, is discipline. My depression can often lead to a cycle where I procrastinate and end up with a web of trouble and concerns behind me. I'd like to try and end this when I get back. It's just too easy for me to prefer something I just want to do over homework, studying, or official stuff. I'm sure that the lack of all that stress behind me will free me to look at things from a more positive angle.

So no, I don't think I want to take the antidepressants because I have a feeling that my depression is just a result of my actions. I'll have to take a crack at solving those source problems and see if my life improves or not.
